description: M3 Normalization (tasks.md T3.1-T3.4, FR-8-FR-11, E-6, E-12). Add pure, deterministic, no-I/O normalization: timezone-aware date/time parsing that flags (never drops) unparseable values, a documented keyword-table food classifier, and a normalizer that maps a SourceRecord's parsed_fields into canonical Event field values while preserving per-source originals. Depends on FEAT-002 for SourceRecord shape.
steps: Create vandy_food_radar/normalize/__init__.py and vandy_food_radar/normalize/datetime_parse.py: parse event_date ('YYYY-MM-DD') to a date and start_time/end_time ('HH:MM') to tz-aware values in config.timezone; return a result that distinguishes a parsed value from an unparseable one (flag it, do not drop, do not raise). Pure, no I/O.

Create vandy_food_radar/normalize/food_classifier.py with a DOCUMENTED keyword table mapping description text to FoodCategory (full_meal: dinner/lunch/breakfast/buffet/meal/pizza; snacks_or_refreshments: refreshments/snacks/coffee/cookies/appetizers/bagels/popcorn) and to FoodConfirmed (explicit free-food/menu -> confirmed; vague -> unconfirmed; neg/absent -> as appropriate incl. contradicted). Deterministic and pure. The classifier must derive category/confirmed independently from text so records without those keys are still classified.

Create vandy_food_radar/normalize/normalizer.py: normalize(record) -> a canonical NormalizedRecord (or partially-filled Event fields) using datetime_parse and food_classifier, PRESERVING the per-source originals (keep them on the SourceRecord.parsed_fields; no lossy overwrite). Derive a per-record cancelled signal from parsed_fields['cancelled'] or a '[CANCELLED]'/status marker. No I/O.

Create tests/test_normalize.py: valid date/time parses; bad date/bad time is flagged not dropped and does not crash; 'Refreshments provided' -> snacks_or_refreshments; the dinner-with-menu fixture -> full_meal + confirmed; missing/null fields tolerated; original per-source values preserved.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer converts each source's parsed_fields into the canonical shape and preserves originals (T3.1, FR-8/9).
Date/time parsing is timezone-aware and flags unparseable values instead of dropping them (T3.2, FR-10, E-12).
Food classifier maps text to full_meal/snacks_or_refreshments/unspecified/none and a confirmed/unconfirmed/contradicted status via a documented table (T3.3, FR-11, E-6).
Normalization functions are pure (no network/DB/file I/O) and deterministic.
uv run pytest tests/test_normalize.py passes and `make check` is green.
findings:
Implemented in vandy_food_radar/normalize/ (datetime_parse.py, food_classifier.py, normalizer.py, __init__.py). All pure/deterministic, no I/O. Import surface: `from vandy_food_radar.normalize import normalize, NormalizedRecord, classify_food, FoodClassification, parse_event_date, parse_event_time, ParsedDate, ParsedTime, FOOD_CATEGORY_KEYWORDS, FOOD_CONFIRMED_KEYWORDS, FOOD_NEGATION_KEYWORDS`.

DATETIME PARSING (datetime_parse.py):
- parse_event_date(raw) -> ParsedDate(ok, value: date|None, raw). Format strictly 'YYYY-MM-DD' via strptime. Missing/malformed => ok=False, value=None, raw preserved. Never raises.
- parse_event_time(raw, timezone) -> ParsedTime(ok, value: time|None, raw). Format strictly 'HH:MM'. Returns a TZ-AWARE datetime.time whose tzinfo is ZoneInfo(timezone). Missing/malformed => ok=False. Never raises.
- resolve_timezone(timezone) -> tzinfo; unknown/blank IANA name falls back to UTC (no raise). NOTE: time carries tzinfo but NOT a date, so it is a fixed-offset stamp; DST correctness would need combining with the date if ever required downstream.

FOOD CLASSIFIER (food_classifier.py): classify_food(description: str|None) -> FoodClassification(category: FoodCategory, confirmed: FoodConfirmed, matched_keywords: tuple[str,...]). Whole-word, case-insensitive regex matching on lowercased text. Documented keyword table exported as constants:
- FOOD_CATEGORY_KEYWORDS[FULL_MEAL] = dinner,lunch,breakfast,brunch,buffet,meal,pizza,bbq,barbecue,tacos,catered,catering; [SNACKS_OR_REFRESHMENTS] = refreshments,snacks,snack,coffee,cookies,appetizers,bagels,popcorn,light bites,desserts,dessert,treats.
- Category resolution: FULL_MEAL keyword wins over snack keyword; else snacks; else non-empty-but-no-keyword => UNSPECIFIED; empty/None => NONE.
- FOOD_CONFIRMED_KEYWORDS: free food/free pizza/lunch|dinner|breakfast, *provided phrases, served, catered, menu => CONFIRMED.
- FOOD_NEGATION_KEYWORDS: no free food/no food/food not provided/byo/bring your own => CONTRADICTED (checked BEFORE confirmed keywords, E-6). Else UNCONFIRMED.

NORMALIZER (normalizer.py): normalize(record: SourceRecord, *, timezone: str) -> NormalizedRecord. Does NOT mutate the input; copies parsed_fields. NormalizedRecord fields: source_id (SourceId), source_record_id (=record.id), parse_status (passthrough), title, event_date: date|None, start_time/end_time: time|None (tz-aware), location, organizer, rsvp_required: bool|None (tri-state, None=unspecified), rsvp_url, event_url, food_confirmed (FoodConfirmed), food_category (FoodCategory), food_description, food_classification (FoodClassification|None), cancelled: bool, date_flagged/start_time_flagged/end_time_flagged: bool, original_fields: dict (VERBATIM copy of record.parsed_fields, preserved per FR-9).
- FOOD PRECEDENCE: a VALID source-declared parsed_fields['food_category']/['food_confirmed'] enum string is preferred over the text-derived classification; invalid/absent falls back to classify_food(food_description). So fixtures that carry these keys keep their declared values; records lacking them are still classified from food_description text.
- FLAGGING (FR-10/E-12): *_flagged is True ONLY when the source supplied a value that failed to parse. A missing/None value is NOT flagged (flagged means 'present but unparseable').
- CANCELLED SIGNAL (E-4): _detect_cancelled returns True if parsed_fields['cancelled'] is True, OR parsed_fields['status']=='cancelled' (case-insensitive), OR title contains '[cancelled]' (CANCELLED_MARKER, case-insensitive). Per-record only; dedup/verify (FEAT-004/005) aggregates to the event-level CANCELLED VerificationState.
- Non-ok parse_status records still normalize (empty canonical fields, originals preserved) — never raises.

DOWNSTREAM NOTES: NormalizedRecord is a per-SOURCE canonical view; dedup groups these by event_date+title similarity, then verify resolves per-field conflicts across a group's NormalizedRecords using authority_precedence and source_updated_at (which lives on SourceRecord, not NormalizedRecord — join back via source_record_id if needed). event_id is still '' at this stage; canonical id assigned by dedup. tests/test_normalize.py (19 tests) green; full make check green (60 tests, ruff+black+mypy --strict clean).
